fields.subnational_unit: Aguas Verdes district, Zarumilla province, Tumbes region (Peru-Ecuador border); period 2018-2020, fieldwork June 2021
fields.population: residents of Aguas Verdes (about 16,000 inhabitants, 4,000 families; 60% with access to drinking water) and institutional actors UESST (service provider), MDAV (district municipality), SUNASS (regulator), MVCS and ANA
fields.sample_size: household survey of 94 residents (finite-population sample formula, 95% confidence, 10% margin) in June 2021; interviews with officials of UESST, MDAV and SUNASS; document review; participatory workshop with community leaders
fields.effect_measure: mixed-methods diagnostic: descriptive survey percentages, institutional interviews and document review on access, coverage, quality, equality of rights and corruption
fields.effect_estimate: 77% of surveyed residents report a household water connection and 68% a sewer connection (23% and 32% without); per the utility, of connected users 67.3% have an active connection, so only 51.8% receive effective service, about 2 hours a day on average (no local water source: water is pumped from the Zarumilla well). 63% are dissatisfied with the water supply (5% satisfied); 80% report no sanitary-education training. SUNASS, despite its regulatory framework for annual inspection, showed no supervision in 2021 and no sanction of the provider UESST for breaching the service-quality regulation; the municipality's sanitation project completed in 2021 had not yet worked; widespread perception of corruption, weak transparency, oversight and participation. Recommends accountability mechanisms and a rights-based approach.
fields.model_type: descriptive survey statistics with institutional interviews, document analysis and a participatory workshop
fields.study_design: mixed-methods case study (survey, interviews, document review, workshop) in one district; Master's thesis
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: CASP Qualitative per-item (re-appraised 2026-10-04 on the full text; supersedes the abstract-only rating of 2026-09-28): 1(aims)=Yes; 2(qual approach)=Yes; 3(design)=Yes (case study of one district with institutional actors named); 4(recruitment)=Yes (sample size computed by the finite-population formula; selection of interviewees by institutional role); 5(data collection)=Yes (survey, interviews, workshop and documents, instruments described); 6(researcher-participant)=Can't tell; 7(ethics)=Can't tell (not located); 8(analysis rigor)=Can't tell (descriptive percentages; no coding detail for interviews); 9(findings)=Yes; 10(value)=Yes. Per CASP's own guidance no composite score is computed.
fields.section: Full text (Spanish; PUCP Master's thesis): Resumen; Marco; Metodologia; Resultados (cobertura, calidad, acceso con enfoque de derechos); Conclusiones
fields.exact_location: Resumen p iv; sample design p7-8; Results 5.1-5.2 p66-70 (Tables 17-22; interviews with SUNASS, MDAV, UESST)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a Master's thesis on inadequate water and sanitation services in Aguas Verdes, Tumbes, Peru (survey n = 94, institutional interviews, workshop), read in full text 2026-10-04. A formal connection rate of 77% falls to 51.8% effective service (about 2 hours a day); the regulator SUNASS showed no supervision or sanction of the provider in 2021; corruption perceptions and weak transparency. Descriptive, single district.
